indexedAssertion.sourceAssertion: Given concurrent real subprocess refresh/add with fake-provider barriers and OS/storage crash cuts, When both orders persist and fresh processes reload, Then the newest accepted refresh generation and added grant survive without a lost update.

sourceFinding: Current add-enospc/add-replace-fault checks inject OSError at the auth.json rename audit event, then assert sanitized save denial and fresh list/chat refusal. They do not terminate a native child at the atomic commit boundary or prove post-restart old-versus-new state. Pinned auth add persists through _save_auth_store → atomic_json_write → _atomic_write: staged file write/flush/fsync, atomic_replace, metadata restore, then directory fsync.

minimumProof.writtenInterfaceChange: None required. Keep the killed child's boundary record in the existing CheckView prerequisite/reason evidence; its fixture JSON result is unavailable by design. Use existing add/list/priority/chat phases and result fields for fresh subprocess readbacks. Do not extend the public CLI or contract enums unless implementation later needs typed returned crash-cut data.
minimumProof.disposableProfile: Reuse runHermesAuthFixture's temporary home, pinned candidate archive and profile created by the public profile command. Restrict the fault to the candidate profile's exact HERMES_HOME/auth.json after fake token response; do not target installed Hermes or global-root auth.json.

faultBoundaries.boundary: At the existing os.rename audit event for the exact disposable profile auth.json, after the staged payload has been flushed and fsynced but before the real replace syscall.
faultBoundaries.action: Signal the existing external barrier and hold the auth-add child there; once the parent observes that exact marker, send SIGKILL and wait for child exit.
faultBoundaries.restartOracle: Run a fresh public auth list and target the unique storage-cut label with public auth priority. The old row count remains and the uncommitted label is absent; the existing grant remains usable.

faultBoundaries.boundary: Wrap only the external os.replace seam for the exact disposable profile auth.json: call the real os.replace, then signal and hold before returning to Hermes, before metadata restoration and directory fsync.
faultBoundaries.action: Once the parent observes the post-replace marker, send SIGKILL and wait for child exit.
faultBoundaries.restartOracle: Fresh public auth list observes one additional row; public auth priority by the unique storage-cut label succeeds at #1; a fresh public chat uses the surviving added grant through the existing fake-provider refresh path and must observe added-rotated with no denials.

minimumProof.sequence: Use a unique deterministic add label so it cannot collide with the earlier concurrency grant. Perform the pre-replace cut and verify absence, then retry that same add in the same disposable profile and perform the post-replace cut. In both cases the add itself is the real public auth add command. The parent records only boundary marker, child signal/exit, sanitized fixture results and public list/priority/chat readbacks; it does not inspect auth.json contents or raw streams.
minimumProof.externalSeam: Extend the existing fixture OS audit seam and barrier directory only. The pre-replace cut uses its registered rename event; the post-replace cut calls the original OS replace before pausing. Do not mock _save_auth_store, atomic_json_write, _atomic_write, CredentialPool collaborators, or private functions. Do not add stale-response ordering work unless an existing AT87 assertion is found to require it.
